cards.prose: Both gospels send the cleansed man to the priest, and both say it is Moses' commandment and not a new one. Matthew calls it *the gift that Moses commanded*. Luke says what the offering is for: *offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded*. Yahusha (Jesus) touches the leper and then sends him straight back into the Torah's own order for a cleansed leper.
cards.member_phrase: shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them
cards.member_sentence: Matthew's Yahusha (Jesus) sends the healed leper to the priest with the gift Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.

cards.prose: Matthew asks whether the wedding guests can *mourn* while the bridegroom is with them, and Luke asks whether you can make them *fast*. It is the same question put to the ones who asked about fasting. Either way he sits in the bridegroom's place, and Isaiah gives that place to Elohim (God): *as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy Elohim (God) rejoice over thee* (Isaiah 62:5).
cards.member_phrase: but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast
cards.member_sentence: Matthew asks whether the guests can mourn while the bridegroom is with them, then says the days will come when he is taken and they fast.

cards.prose: Luke has a piece of new cloth on an old garment, and Matthew's verse has *new wine into old bottles*. It is one saying told with two figures. Put the new into something too worn to hold it and the garment tears and the bottles burst, but *they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved*. Both figures are about what a vessel can hold.
cards.member_phrase: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved
cards.member_sentence: Matthew's wine and bottles carry the same lesson as Luke's cloth: the new is not put into what cannot hold it, and both are preserved.
cards.flag: Old note grouped this with leaven and read it as the new heart; Luke 5:36 is the garment and the target is wine and bottles, so I wrote the figure itself.
